full_judgment: 35. Let us now direct our attention to the second branch of contention raised from the side of the informant-appellant that the learned Tribunal illegally and improperly rejected a Certificate issued by the Headmaster, Uthali Government Primary School, Shibalaya, Manikganj in proof of the case that Anjali Rani was born on 27-8-1980. The provision of section 428 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and section 167 of the Evidence Act had been also relied upon in support of a further contention that to secure the ends of justice, this Court in the exercise of the appellate power can admit the said Certificate in evidence. The contention so raised appears to be without any substance. Section 167 of the Evidence Act enjoins that if any evidence is improperly admitted or improperly rejected that will not itself be a ground for new trial or reversal of any decision in any case if the decision of the court can be supported by other evidences on record. The provision of section 167 of the Evidence Act is not at all applicable and the same is misquoted.
